title: Skills are static and dynamic context
caption: What's always loaded is static; a skill loads on demand, so it is dynamic.

alt.room: The control room at the end of the dive. On the wall: the live camera feed from the robot at the seabed, the project brief and the manual on its shelf with its index page facing out. At the desk the pilot sits; on the desk his notebook of standing orders, and everything that arrived during the dive: the pulled procedure card, Collect sediment sample, propped and lit; printed camera frames; a sonar strip; and a sample log on a clipboard.

static-and-dynamic-as-google-defines-the.header: Static and dynamic, as Google defines them
static-and-dynamic-as-google-defines-the.description: Static context is always loaded: system instructions, rule files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md), global memory and persona definitions; dynamic context is loaded on demand: skill instructions triggered by task matching, tool results, retrieved documents and windowed session history [1]. This is Google's vendor framing of the vendors' own mechanics, not a measured result.

google-day-1-new-sdlc.title: Osmani, Saboo and Kartakis, The New SDLC With Vibe Coding (Google whitepaper, Kaggle)

why-static-and-dynamic-context-are-kept-.header: Why static and dynamic context are kept apart
why-static-and-dynamic-context-are-kept-.description: Day 1 says static context “is expensive because every token is present in every interaction, regardless of relevance”, and that too much of it “wastes tokens and dilutes signals” while too little “means the agent forgets critical rules” [1]. Day 3 repeats the split for the two files: “From one side AGENTS.md is always loaded within the project; Skills load on demand.” [2]

static-instructions-are-a-rule-of-thumb.header: Static instructions are a rule of thumb
static-instructions-are-a-rule-of-thumb.description: Instructions are not strictly static. Claude Code .claude/rules/ files with paths load only when matching files open [1], Gemini CLI loads further GEMINI.md files just in time when a tool touches a directory [2], and Copilot path-specific instructions apply by file match [3]. By default, a skill's name and description are always loaded too, unless the skill is set to user-only invocation [4].

back-to-the-window.title: Back to the window
back-to-the-window.script: Some of you have seen the context window Explorable, where we looked at everything the model holds in its head at once. This is the same context window, and now we place skills in it.

the-standing-part.title: The standing part
the-standing-part.script: Start with what is there before any task begins, in the order the Explorable shows it: the system prompt, the skills, meaning the name and description of every skill, and the memory files, meaning your instructions in AGENTS.md. On our ship that is the standing rules, the manual's index, and your standing orders and the project brief. That part is static, so it sits in the window whatever the task turns out to be.

filling-as-you-dive.title: Filling as you dive
filling-as-you-dive.script: Then the task begins and the window fills up: the skill the model opened, and the tool results it gets back, the camera frames, sonar readings and sample logs of the dive. That part is dynamic, and a skill's instructions belong to it, whether you call the skill at the start or the model picks it halfway through. So a skill sits on both sides of the line: its name and description are static, and the skill itself is dynamic.
